findings.title: Configured attachment size limits are ignored
findings.body: This replaces the per-type `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` limits with a fixed 10 MB limit. Attachments are not downsized, so sites that allow attachments larger than 10 MB will now reject them in the browser even though the server is configured to accept them. Preserve the configured attachment limit and apply any fixed cap only where intended.

findings.title: Downsizing can discard animated GIF frames
findings.body: When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the non-animated downsize instructions, which read only `from[0]`. Because this call overwrites the uploaded file, an oversized animated GIF is reduced to its first frame and loses its animation. Thumbnail animation preferences should not cause destructive changes to the uploaded original.

findings.title: The new `downsize` definition breaks the existing dimensions API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by arity: this definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition. Existing callers that pass separate width and height values will now pass the height as `opts` or raise an argument error, breaking downsizing. Retain support for the old call signature while accepting the new geometry-string form.
